thread:
elaine-cs: Heads-up — Acme flagged a production endpoint: quantized (4-bit) variant is slower than FP16 since yesterday evening. They see higher tail latency and quality complaints. Attachments: customer logs + sample request.

jordan-runtime: ack. Can you paste the customer p95/p99 numbers and sample payload?

elaine-cs: p50: 110ms, p95: 1.4s, p99: 2.8s for quant-4bit. FP16 baseline for same timeframe was p50: 90ms, p95: 400ms, p99: 650ms. Sample prompt is a 1.2k token chat history. Customer says latency increase started after we rolled quant dispatch change yesterday.

vikram-ml: interesting — likely interaction between KV cache policy and our int4 kernels. Quick hypothesis: quantized kernel avoids fused KV-cache path and ends up rebuilding KV repeatedly for generation, so per-token cost spikes for long histories.

jordan-runtime: I pulled the runtime traces from their endpoint:
```
[kernel_select] model=gpt-medium quant=4bit seq=1200 selected_kernel=int4_attention_v2 (no-kvfast)
[batch_assembler] batch_window_ms=8 max_batch=16 observed_batch=1
[kv_cache] hits=0.12 misses=0.88 average_kv_recompute_tokens=1100
```
Looks like batcher collapsed to single-request batches and KV misses high.

maya-sre: NVTX trace shows heavy memcpy and kernel launch overhead for int4 path vs fp16. nvprof snippet:
```
GPU memcpy HtoD: 12ms
int4_attention_v2 kernel: 9ms (per step) * 1200 steps
fp16_attention kernel: 5ms (per step) * 1200 steps
```
This matches higher end-to-end.

vikram-ml: Two things to confirm: 1) whether quant kernel supports the fast KV append/merge path and 2) if calibration happened with long sequences. If calibration used short sequences, scale factors could be off and trigger slower fallback loops.

jordan-runtime: I repro'd locally with a similar seq length and saw same: int4 path selected `int4_attention_v2` which doesn't use our optimized KV-merge codepath (we have a note in kernel registry). When forced to `int4_attention_v2_kvmerge` latency drops ~40%.

ana-ops: quick mitigation options for customer? They need immediate relief.

jordan-runtime: short-term: pin that endpoint to FP16 model variant (fastest to roll). Another short-term: disable KV caching for quant variant so it uses fused per-step kernels (not ideal for cost). Medium-term: enable the `int4_attention_v2_kvmerge` kernel and add a hotfix to kernel-selector to prefer KV-merge when seq_len>256 and kv_cache=true.

vikram-ml: Also add a calibration job: run dynamic calibration with long context (1k tokens) and include representative payloads. Bad calibration can cause dequantization overheads.

elaine-cs: Customer asked for ETA on rollback/pin. We can pin to FP16 immediately; do we need approvals?

ana-ops: No approvals for a config pin for a single tenant. I'll patch their routing to FP16 in the control plane and notify.

jordan-runtime: I'll create a patch branch for kernel-selector and a canary deploy. Plan: (A) control-plane pin to FP16 now, (B) enable int4 kv-merge kernel behind flag + run canary on internal traffic, (C) run calibration job, (D) push canary for customer to test int4-kvmerge.

maya-sre: Scheduling: pin now (~5m), canary build for kernel-selector in 2 hours, calibration experiment tomorrow morning, customer update after pin (CC:elaine).

deploy-bot: deploy:controlplane patch queued by ana-ops — change: route acme/endpoint-237 -> model:fp16/gpt-medium:v3. ETA ~ 3m.

elaine-cs: Sending customer note: "We've pinned your endpoint to FP16 to restore tail latency; engineering is investigating a quant/KV interaction and will follow up with a plan and timeline." :white_check_mark:

jordan-runtime: For the engineering ticket I'll include: kernel registry mismatch, batcher heuristics causing single-request batches for quant path, calibration sweep missing long contexts, and proposed fixes (kv-merge kernel enable, batching window tuning, calibration).

vikram-ml: One more action: add a perf regression test comparing fp16 vs quantized variants on long-contexts to CI. Prevents future rollouts.

elaine-cs: Thanks team. I'll keep the customer updated.

maya-sre: filed incident follow-up doc and perf traces under /observability/1770018100/acme-quant-kv-incident.

jordan-runtime: assigning to me + vikram for root-cause. I'll create the PR for kernel-selector flag and link here.

vikram-ml: spotted a small note — if we enable kv-merge kernel we must ensure it supports 4-bit accumulation without precision regression. I'll run quality tests as part of the canary.

elaine-cs: closing loop: customer acknowledged the pin and saw p95 drop to ~420ms within 10 minutes. They appreciate the quick fix.
